say: Welcome to Market Day, inquirers! Today you are shoppers AND shopkeepers. You will pay exactly, give change, and find every way to pay without missing one.
Notice it, test it with play money, and explain why.
Here is our market. The sticker book costs $3.45. That means 3 dollars and 45 cents. Pay exactly with your play money.
Now count your pieces. Who used the fewest? How did you choose?
The toy stall has a kite, a ball, a yo-yo, bubbles and a sticker. You have $10. How many different baskets do you think cost EXACTLY $10? Write a guess.
stuck: Stuck: start with the most expensive toy. Put it in the basket. How much is left to spend?
Repeating baskets: “Kite and ball is the same basket as ball and kite.”
Finished early: which basket gives you the most toys for $10? Which gives exactly $1 change?

say: “Ways to pay $6 with $5 notes, $2 notes and $1 coins. I start with the biggest note: one $5. $1 is left, so one $1 coin. Now no $5: three $2, then two $2 and two $1, one $2 and four $1, no $2 and six $1. The $2 column went 3, 2, 1, 0, so I know I am finished: 5 ways.”
“Mei spent 80¢ on a drink, then 65¢ on a bun, and has 55¢ left. I work backwards from the end. Before the bun she had 55 + 65 = 120¢. Before the drink she had 120 + 80 = 200¢. That is $2.”
“Change from $1 for 45¢: I count on like a shopkeeper. 45¢ and 5¢ is 50¢. 50¢ and 50¢ is $1. So the change is 5¢ + 50¢ = 55¢.”

do: Ask: “Is this in cents or in dollars? How do you know?”
Ask: “What is the biggest note that is not too much?”
Ask: “How do you know you have found every way?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Lay out real play money and count it.”
Hint 2: “Make a table with a column for each note or coin. Start with as many of the biggest as you can.”
Hint 3: “Start from the money that is left and put back what was spent.”

do: Ask: “Is this in cents or in dollars? How do you know?”
Ask: “What is the biggest note that is not too much?”
Ask: “How do you know you have found every way?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Lay out real play money and count it.”
Hint 2: “Make a table with a column for each note or coin. Start with as many of the biggest as you can.”
Hint 3: “Start from the money that is left and put back what was spent.”

say: “Mei says: To pay $40 with the fewest notes, I use two $20 notes. What would you tell her?”
ask: “Mei says: To pay $40 with the fewest notes, I use two $20 notes. What would you tell her?”
There is no $20 note in Singapore. $50 is too much, so we use $10 notes: $10 + $10 + $10 + $10, which is 4 notes.

say: “Great shopping, inquirers! You paid exactly, gave change and made lists in order. A good shopkeeper always checks, and so did you.”

p2l6-title.note: Objective: Read and write money in dollars and cents, pay exactly with the fewest notes and coins, make a list in order to find every way to pay, give change by counting on, decide whether there is enough money, and work backwards to find how much someone had at first. Materials: play money (coins 5¢, 10¢, 20¢, 50¢, $1; notes $2, $5, $10, $50), about 6 of each per pair, price tags, mini whiteboards. Online: print the cut-out coins and notes, or use real money at home; the shop and toy stall are on the slides and children count their money aloud and say the total together on three. Time plan: opening 0 to 1.5, sneak-peek puzzles 1.5 to 6, warm-up 6 to 10.5, explore 10.5 to 23.5, mini-lesson 23.5 to 35.5, brain break 35.5 to 38.5, worksheet teach slide 38.5 to 41, worksheet page 1 41 to 52.5, check together, page 1 52.5 to 55, short teaching 55 to 59.5, worksheet page 2 59.5 to 71, check together, page 2 71 to 73.5, flex (spare time) 73.5 to 76.5, talk time 76.5 to 81.5, exit ticket 81.5 to 86.5, looking back 86.5 to 88.5, closing and stamps 88.5 to 90. The Think harder and Go further slides are optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Kit ready at minute 0: ask families to put every item on the desk before the lesson starts (a 30-second check at the start). SPINE: Today's tool is List every way. Write each way down, in order, so none is missed. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l6-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is List every way. Write each way down, in order, so none is missed. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l6-precheck.note: Minutes 1.5 to 6. Sneak-peek puzzles: two puzzles on the key idea of today, which the children have NOT learnt yet. Say out loud (about 28 words): "Two sneak-peek puzzles on ideas we have not learnt yet. Guessing is welcome, so is I do not know. Nobody is marked. Say your answer together on three." Question 1 is an access question: any child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone has a first win (about 45 seconds). Question 2 is the thinking question (about 90 seconds). Then about 2 minutes for the answers slide and the move on. Answers are PRIVATE: each child writes on their own paper and says the answer together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Do not raise whiteboards together, do not read answers out, do not name children. Q1 answer: 80¢ (50 + 20 + 10). Listen for: Counting on from the biggest coin. This is a first win for everyone. Q2 answer: Yes. 3 drinks cost $4.80, so 20¢ is left. Listen for: Listen for adding $1.60 three times, or $1 + $1 + $1 and then 60¢ three times (180¢ = $1.80). Counting up from $4.80 to $5 is a good method. At the end click to show the answers as "one way to think about it", without saying who had what. Ask only for volunteers: "Would anyone like to tell us how they started?" Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Never announce who is on which page. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Children can move either way at any time. Everyone joins explore, the mini-lesson, the check-together slides and talk time.

p2l6-warm1.note: Minutes 6 to 8.5. The Market Day shop, two price tags only: the eraser (85¢) and the scooter ($57.20). The play money is already cut out and on the desk (kit at minute 0). Point to one item at a time: "The eraser costs 85 cents. Pay exactly. Can you use fewer pieces than your partner?" Children lay out their money; click to show the fewest way (clicks go Eraser, Scooter). Fewest: 85¢ = 50¢ + 20¢ + 10¢ + 5¢ (4). $57.20 = $50 + $5 + $2 + 20¢ (4). (Spare tags, not shown: $1.35 = $1 + 20¢ + 10¢ + 5¢ (4); $3.45 = $2 + $1 + 20¢ + 20¢ + 5¢ (5); $6.50 = $5 + $1 + 50¢ (3); $12.70 = $10 + $2 + 50¢ + 20¢ (4).) Strategy to draw out: pay the dollars first with the biggest note that is not too much, then the cents with the biggest coin that fits. Ask: "Someone paid 85¢ with eight 10¢ coins and a 5¢ coin. Is it exact? Is it the fewest?" (Exact, yes. Fewest, no: 9 pieces instead of 4.) Watch for 50¢ and $50 mixed up. A game of about 2.5 minutes: stop it on the clock even if the game is not finished.

p2l6-warm2.note: Minutes 8.5 to 10.5. Whiteboards, then click. 1) 345¢ is 300¢ and 45¢: $3 and 45¢. 2) $1.50 is 150¢, which is more than 105¢. Spare questions in the guide table: $2.05 is 205¢ (watch for 25¢ or 250¢); 75¢ is 50¢ + 20¢ + 5¢, 3 coins; 60¢ to 85¢ is 25¢ more (count on). Ask quick questions 1 and 3 only (about 2 minutes): children answer by thumbs, hands, not by naming a child. The other questions are spare.

p2l6-explore1.note: Minutes 10.5 to 19.5. Each pair gets a $10 note and the price list: kite $6, ball $4, yo-yo $3, bubbles $2, sticker $1 (whole dollars, so children add in dollars only). They go straight to hunting for every basket that costs exactly $10 (the change idea comes in the debrief). Pair work is 5.5 minutes. Prediction first: "How many $10 baskets do you think there are?" Online: the stall is on the slide; children record baskets on whiteboards. Hint for stuck pairs: "Put the kite in first. How much is left to spend?" Go further (a second what-if, so nobody waits) is the box at the foot of this slide; the question is also posted in the chat when the pairs go to their breakout rooms. It is for ANY child who finishes the explore task or wants more: say it to the whole group as a choice, never as a prize, and never name who tries it. Pairs stay together unless both children agree to split. Answer: 5 baskets: kite + ball; kite + yo-yo + sticker; ball + sticker + robot; yo-yo + bubbles + robot; ball + yo-yo + bubbles + sticker. Take it at the debrief only if a pair offers it.

p2l6-explore2.note: Minutes 19.5 to 23.5. Gather the pairs. Answers: 1) 3 baskets: kite + ball ($6 + $4); kite + yo-yo + sticker ($6 + $3 + $1); ball + yo-yo + bubbles + sticker ($4 + $3 + $2 + $1). 2) Work in order: first all baskets WITH the kite ($4 more to spend: ball, or yo-yo + sticker, since bubbles + sticker is only $3 and yo-yo + bubbles is $5), then baskets WITHOUT the kite (the other four toys cost $10 altogether, so all four is the only one). 3) $6 + $2 = $8, so $2 change. Keep it moving (about 4 minutes in all): ask "how do you know?" on question 2 only; about 15 seconds of talk on the other questions.

p2l6-teach1.note: Minutes 23.5 to 25.5. Teach. Hold up $3 in notes and coins and 45¢ in coins: "This is 3 dollars and 45 cents. We write $3.45." Count it all in cents with the children: 100, 200, 300, then 320, 340, 345. Then the trap: $3.05 and $3.50 look alike but 5¢ and 50¢ are very different. Ask: "How do you write 2 dollars and 8 cents?" ($2.08).

p2l6-we1.note: Minutes 25.5 to 28.5. Click to build each row and the side notes. Ask before each row: "What comes next if I use one fewer $2?" Think-aloud: "One $5 and one $1. Now no $5: three $2 makes $6. Two $2 makes $4, so two $1. One $2 and four $1. Six $1 coins. The $2 column counts down to 0, so I know I have them all: 5 ways." Point out $5 + $1 and $1 + $5 are the same way.

p2l6-try1.note: Minutes 28.5 to 29.5. Whiteboards. One item: 20 + 20; 20 + 10 + 10; four 10¢. Ask: "How do you know there are no more?" (the 20¢ coins go 2, 1, 0.) Items b and c are dropped: worksheet Q1 and Q2 have the same types.

p2l6-we2.note: Minutes 29.5 to 32.5. Click through. The bar shows all her money cut into what she spent and what is left, so "at first" is the whole bar. Think-aloud: "The last thing she did was buy the bun, so I put the bun money back first." Ask: "How do we write 200¢ in dollars?" ($2, or $2.00).

p2l6-try2.note: Minutes 32.5 to 34.5. Whiteboards. a) $10 − $4 = $6 (check: $6 + $4 = $10). b) 40¢ + 35¢ = 75¢. (The old item c, Ravi and the half, is dropped: it is Think harder.)

p2l6-key.note: Minutes 34.5 to 35.5. Say the key ideas together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Mixing up dollars and cents: 345¢ written as $34.5, or $3.05 read as $3.50. (2) Using a $20 note, or not starting with the biggest note that fits when finding the fewest. (3) Listing ways with no order, so some are missed or written twice.

p2l6-break.note: Minutes 35.5 to 38.5. Three minutes: two of movement, one for a drink of water. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place.

p2l6-teachfew.note: Minutes 38.5 to 41. Teach before worksheet page 1 (Q1 has four prices to pay with the fewest pieces). Model with play money. Stress: $20 is two $10 notes. Ask: "Could $27 use fewer than 4 notes?" (No: no single note or pair of notes makes $27 without a $20 note.) Do not do the worksheet prices.

p2l6-ws1.note: Minutes 41 to 52.5. Walk around. Ask "How do you know you have them all?" Check that pairs start Q2 with one $5 note and then count the $2 notes down. The last row of Q1 (the bicycle, $76) and Q2(b) are marked ★ take-home on the page: children do them at home. Say once, to everyone: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never say who is on which page. Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Pairs are not split unless both children agree.

p2l6-ws1ans.note: Minutes 52.5 to 55. Click after pairs explain (answer lines only). The $76 row and Q2(b) are take-home stars: the answers stay here so children can mark them at home. Q2 table ($5, $2, $1): 1,1,1 / 1,0,3 / 0,4,0 / 0,3,2 / 0,2,4 / 0,1,6 / 0,0,8. Row H stays empty. With one $5 there is $3 left: one $2 + one $1, or three $1. With no $5 the $2 column goes 4, 3, 2, 1, 0. Pieces: 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.

p2l6-teachchange.note: Minutes 55 to 57. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q3). Act it out: one child is the shopkeeper and counts the change into Ali’s hand: "33 … 35, 40, 50." Check with take-away: $50 − $33 = $17. Watch for children who give $27 (counting the wrong way).

p2l6-teachenough.note: Minutes 57 to 58.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q4). "Is there enough?" means: add the prices, then compare with the money. (Listing ALL the pairs for an exact change is worksheet Q4(b), a take-home star: not taught here.) Do not do the worksheet prices.

p2l6-teachlist2.note: Minutes 58.5 to 59.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q6 uses stickers and erasers at different prices). Ask for each row: "Can 20¢ pencils make exactly the amount left?" Count in 20s: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. 10¢ and 70¢ are not in the count, so those rows do not work. Four erasers would cost $1.20, too much, so we start at 3.

p2l6-ws2.note: Minutes 59.5 to 71. Children work alone. Q3(b) (change from $50) and Q4(b) (pairs with $3 change) are marked ★ take-home on the page: children do them at home. Note who needs a short catch-up next lesson. Check that Q6 is a list in order, not guesses. Tutor rule at minute 59.5: if the clock is more than 2 minutes late, drop the last Core question of page 2 to take-home (children draw a star beside it). Never shorten talk time, the exit ticket, looking back or the closing. Questions marked with a star and the words take-home on the page are done at home; their answers are still on the check-together slide.

p2l6-ws2ans.note: Minutes 71 to 73.5. Click after a child explains (answer lines only). Q3(b) and Q4(b) are take-home stars: the answers stay here so children can mark them at home. Q3b: count on $26 → $30 → $40 → $50, or $50 − $26 = $24; no $20 note, so two $10 and two $2. Q4b: she spends $20 − $3 = $17: book + cap = $17, bag + pen = $17; the other four pairs cost $12, $23, $11 and $22. Q5a: 25 + 30 + 45 = 100¢. Q5b (Think harder 1): $6 + $4 = $10 is half, so $20. Q6: 1 or 3 erasers leave 150¢ or 50¢, not in the 20¢ count.

p2l6-stretch.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Open to any child who chooses it (the choice after question 3 on the worksheet). These are the SAME four questions as the printed Think harder page: the slide shows 1 to 3 and question 4 is on the page only. Never announce who is working on which page. Answers: 1) $20 ($6 + $4 = $10 is the half he kept after the kite, so the other half is also $10: $10 + $10 = $20). 2) 10 ways (1 + 3 + 6) 3) 2 sets: $1 + 10¢ + 10¢ + 5¢, and 50¢ + 50¢ + 20¢ + 5¢ 4) (Question: How many different ways can you pay exactly 40¢ using 5¢, 10¢ and 20¢ coins? Make a list in order, starting with the most 20¢ coins.) 9 ways: two 20¢ (1 way); one 20¢ and 20¢ more (3 ways); no 20¢ (5 ways).

p2l6-challenge.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Pairs try first, then the "see it" slide, then the walk-through. Answers: 1) Five 10¢ and five 20¢ (50¢ + 100¢ = 150¢). The totals are $1.00, $1.10, … $2.00 (11 totals, going up 10¢ at a time); $1.55 is not possible because every total is a multiple of 10¢. 2) Sweet, lollipop, jelly and biscuit: 15 + 20 + 25 + 30 = 90¢, with 10¢ change. All five cost $1.35, too much, and any 4 snacks with the chips cost at least $1.05.

p2l6-chdiag.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Show after pairs have tried, or if they are stuck. The pictures show the problem, not the answer. Ask: What changes each time we swap one 10¢ for a 20¢? (The total goes up by 10¢; there are still 10 coins.) For Q2: If you want MANY snacks, which ones should you choose first?

p2l6-chwalk.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Use after pairs have tried. Q1: the swap idea is a list in order (10 and 0, 9 and 1, 8 and 2 …) with the total going up by 10¢ each row. Q2: to get the MOST things, buy the cheapest things first. Ask: "Could she swap the biscuit for the chips?" (15 + 20 + 25 + 45 = 105¢, too much.)

p2l6-talk.note: Minutes 76.5 to 81.5. Pairs talk for 90 seconds, then two volunteers share. Answer: there is no $20 note in Singapore. $50 is too much, so we use four $10 notes. Praise the reasons, not only the answers. Talk time rules: you choose volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"); never cold-call a child by name; any child may say pass; no public tallies, scores or rankings.

p2l6-exit.note: Minutes 81.5 to 86.5. Answer: $2 + $1 + 50¢ + 10¢ + 5¢ (5 pieces). Extension: find every way to pay exactly $10 using $5 notes, $2 notes and $1 coins (there are 10). Children keep slips on their desks and tick them against the answer on the next click; nothing is held up. About 2 minutes of child work.

p2l6-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 86.5 to 88.5. Start the timer (90 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88.5 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
